items.title: MoG-VLM: Efficient Video Anomaly Detection through Motion-Guided Vision-Language Models
items.summary_1line: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have shown strong potential for video anomaly detection, but dense frame-level inference makes them impractical for real-time deployment. Existing acceleration commonly relies on uniform...
items.editor_note: Uses motion guidance to cut the dense frame-level inference that makes VLM video anomaly detection impractical in real time.

items.title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
items.summary_1line: Few-shot industrial anomaly detection requires modeling category-specific normality from only a handful of defect-free images. Common approaches tie inference to stored exemplars, impose rigid linear structure, or ris...
items.editor_note: Few-shot industrial defect detection that avoids stored exemplars and rigid linear structure via single-step conditional-mean recovery.

items.title: LogCDM: Interpretable Log Anomaly Detection via Behavioral Graph Drift and Adaptive Signal Fusion
items.summary_1line: Log-based anomaly detection is increasingly dominated by large pretrained models, from BERT-scale encoders to 8B-parameter language models, which require GPUs at inference time and are difficult to deploy on the monit...
items.editor_note: Moves log anomaly detection off GPU-bound pretrained models to interpretable behavioral-graph drift with adaptive signal fusion.

items.title: Vendi Anomaly Scores for Efficient and Accurate Anomaly Detection
items.summary_1line: Anomaly detection (AD) is a critical for trustworthy machine learning and scientific discovery. Existing methods typically define anomalies through local density, isolation heuristics, or distance from a fitted distri...
items.editor_note: Proposes a diversity-based (Vendi) anomaly score as an alternative to density, isolation and distance-from-distribution definitions.

editorial.tldr: This thread is a label, not one event: four unrelated arXiv papers that share the words "anomaly detection". The October pair targeted video and few-shot industrial inspection, and the August papers it replaced covered relational data, ICS security and streaming video.
editorial.whats_new: Two Nov 9 papers push anomaly detection toward cheaper inference: LogCDM flags log anomalies from behavioral-graph drift without GPU-bound language models, and Vendi Anomaly Scores proposes a diversity-based score in place of density or isolation heuristics.
editorial.why_it_matters: The shared direction is cost: three of the four papers explicitly target cheaper or lighter detection than dense VLM, exemplar-store or 8B-parameter log models, which is the constraint that decides whether a detector can run inside a monitoring or agent pipeline.
editorial.take_for_builders: Read LogCDM if your log anomaly detection needs GPU-hosted models today; skip the rest unless you run video or visual inspection, and wait for released code before planning a swap.

beats.headline: October papers trim the inference cost of vision anomaly detection
beats.summary: MoG-VLM uses motion cues to avoid dense frame-level VLM inference; Flownomaly models normality from a handful of defect-free images without tying inference to stored exemplars.

beats.headline: November papers target log monitoring and a new general-purpose anomaly score
beats.summary: LogCDM argues large pretrained log models are hard to deploy on monitoring hosts and offers an interpretable graph-drift alternative; Vendi Anomaly Scores redefines anomalies by diversity rather than density, isolation or distance.

open_questions: Does LogCDM match the detection accuracy of BERT-scale or 8B-parameter log models on standard log benchmarks while running CPU-only?
Does Vendi Anomaly Scores hold up on high-dimensional embedding data such as LLM traces, or only on the benchmarks the paper reports?
Does MoG-VLM report end-to-end latency on real-time video, or only reduced frame counts?
Do any of these papers release code an operator could run against production telemetry?
